subject: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask
body:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM
Subject: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

Team — I’m trying to unblock the control-plane design so we can staff it properly for Weeks 3–6.

Open decision we keep circling: where does gate evaluation live?

Option A) Gate evaluation embedded in policy engine (per-request / per-route evaluation)
- Pro: single place for routing decision, fewer moving parts
- Con: policy engine becomes stateful + needs metric query access; also makes audits of “why did we advance” messy

Option B) Separate server-side evaluator service (periodic evaluation windows; produces GateEvaluation + StageDecision events)
- Pro: clearer state machine + audit trail; can do “pause on missing metrics” deterministically
- Con: new service + reliability surface; policy engine needs to consume staged weights + “hold” state

Given Dedicated pools + SLAs, I’m leaning B but want a sanity check from policy/routing + SRE + security.

Two asks:
1) Can Ethan/Jordan align on where we land for ADR-027 by end of week?
2) If we choose B, I need a resourcing plan: who owns evaluator implementation vs policy integration vs SLOs?

Attaching my notes + current control-plane diagram.

Attachments:
- staged-rollouts-control-plane-arch-v0.2.pdf
- gate-evaluator-options-notes.txt

Priya

—

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:03 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

Agree the decision is blocking.

My take:
- For Dedicated staged rollouts, “advance/pause/rollback” is a control-plane workflow, not a per-request routing decision.
- Policy engine should read a precomputed routing plan: (pool_id, route_id) -> {weights by stage, pinned model version, hold state}.
- Evaluator should run on a fixed tick + evaluation windows; it emits an “advance allowed” or “hold required” along with the evidence.

If we embed evaluation in the policy engine:
- we either query metrics inline (latency + timeouts) which I don’t want in the hot path
- or we cache metric aggregates in policy engine anyway (so… we built an evaluator, just in the wrong place)

I’m strongly in favor of B.

Resourcing suggestion:
- Control-plane team (Benji/Michael) own data model + persistence + state transitions
- Jordan’s team owns deterministic routing consumption + enforcement (stage weights + hold)
- Logan’s team owns metric query plumbing + aggregation semantics; evaluator consumes it
- SRE sign-off on failure modes + “pause on missing” defaults

Ethan

—

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 12:26 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

+1 to keeping policy engine stateless and fast.

One nuance: even with B, we need to be careful about “who is source of truth” for stage progression.

My strong preference:
- evaluator writes decisions to control plane (RolloutPlanExecution / StageStatus)
- policy engine reads only control-plane state and applies deterministically

What I don’t want:
- evaluator pushing weights directly into policy engine config (another config channel to reconcile)

Also, if evaluator is down, policy engine must fail safe (don’t advance). It can keep routing according to current stage weights, but we should NOT auto-advance on stale “advance allowed” tokens.

Resourcing: I can commit 1 eng (part-time) for the integration + deterministic bucketing behavior, but not for building/operating a new metrics query system. That needs to come from telemetry/observability.

Jordan

—

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 2:18 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

Telemetry POV:

We can support B as long as we constrain gate query patterns.

Constraints we’ll need:
- low-cardinality dimensions (pool_id yes; tenant_id probably yes; route_id yes; model_version maybe; no per-request labels)
- minimum evaluation window sizes (e.g., >= 5m) + step sizes to avoid hammering the TSDB
- explicit “metrics freshness” gate: evaluator should check ingest lag and fail safe

If we embed in policy engine, you’ll either:
- make the policy engine depend on TSDB availability (bad)
- or replicate aggregates into policy engine storage (still a service)

Resourcing: I can spare Caleb 1–2 weeks to help define the metric spec + safe PromQL patterns, but I can’t fully staff ENG-5124 from telemetry alone. We’ll need an owner in platform (control-plane or routing) to build the evaluator loop; telemetry can be a collaborator.

Logan

—

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 4:07 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

SRE input:

Dedicated rollouts need a clear “stop-the-line” lever.

Option B is safer operationally if we define these failure modes up front:
1) Missing metrics / delayed metrics: HOLD, not advance (and ideally surface “why” to Console)
2) Evaluator lagging behind tick schedule: HOLD (don’t advance). Keep current routing weights.
3) TSDB / metrics backend degraded: HOLD (same as missing metrics)
4) Control plane degraded: policy engine must keep last-known-good stage weights; but block new approvals/advancement

If evaluation is inside policy engine, it becomes much harder to answer incident questions like:
- “what evidence caused the stage to advance?”
- “who approved stage 2 and what gates passed at the time?”

Resourcing ask: we’ll need at least one engineer thinking about the oncall shape of evaluator + dashboards/alerts from day 1. Allison isn’t on this thread but will want to review alerting once you pick the design.

Sean

—

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:31 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

Security/compliance angle:

B is easier to make auditable.

We need a durable audit trail of:
- what gate thresholds were configured at the time
- what metric aggregates were observed (or at least a reference to the query + window + evaluated value)
- who/what approved advancement (actor + role + timestamp)
- automatic holds/rollbacks with reason codes

If evaluation happens in policy engine with inline metric fetch, you’ll still need to persist the “evidence” somewhere to satisfy enterprise asks (SUP-3981 style). That persistence becomes its own system anyway.

So from my side: choose B and make sure the evaluator writes structured evaluation records that can be exported.

Marcus

—

From: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 10:02 AM
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

If we’re converging on B, can we explicitly assign a DRI for ENG-5124 (evaluator service)?

Right now my RACI has:
- Control-plane primitives: Ethan/Benji
- Routing enforcement: Jordan/Mina
- Telemetry spec: Logan
- Dashboards/alerts: Sean/Allison

But ENG-5124 is sitting between teams.

Priya — can you propose an owner + % allocation so I can update the program plan today?

Talia

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Talia Benson <talia.benson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: Dedicated staged rollouts: gate evaluation placement + resourcing ask

Thanks all — consistent feedback across Eng/SRE/Sec: go with Option B (server-side evaluator) with policy engine reading control-plane state.

Decision (for ADR-027 draft):
- Evaluator runs on a fixed cadence, evaluates gates over configured windows, and writes GateEvaluation + StageDecision records into control plane.
- Policy engine/routing consumes only control-plane stage state/weights and enforces deterministically.
- Fail-safe defaults: missing/late metrics => HOLD; evaluator degraded => HOLD; no automatic stage advancement on stale evaluations.

Resourcing / DRI:
- DRI ENG-5124: Ethan will assign an engineer from control plane to implement the evaluator loop + persistence writes (Ethan to confirm name by EOD Fri).
- Telemetry collaboration: Logan/Caleb for metric query patterns + freshness checks (timeboxed 1–2 weeks).
- SRE sign-off + dashboards: Sean to review failure modes + alerting requirements before dogfood.
- Security: Marcus to review audit event schema once we have a concrete GateEvaluation record format.

Talia — please update the program plan with the above. I’ll start the ADR-027 doc with Ethan/Jordan’s language and share for comments tomorrow.

Priya

Priya Natarajan
Director, Platform Architecture
